definitions.explanation: Moral wrongdoing or the concept of evil, as opposed to good.

examples.japanese: {善|ぜん}と{悪|あく}の{区別|くべつ}。
examples.english: The distinction between good and evil.

examples.japanese: {悪|あく}に{染|そ}まった{人間|にんげん}を{救|すく}うのは{難|むずか}しい。
examples.english: It is difficult to save a person who has fallen into wickedness.

examples.japanese: この{物語|ものがたり}では、{悪|あく}が{最後|さいご}に{滅|ほろ}びて{正義|せいぎ}が{勝|か}つという{展開|てんかい}になっている。
examples.english: In this story, evil is destroyed in the end and justice prevails.

notes:
{悪|あく} refers to evil or wickedness as an abstract concept. It is the opposite of {善|ぜん} (good/virtue).

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {善|ぜん}と{悪|あく}: good and evil
- {悪|あく}に{染|そ}まる: to be tainted by evil
- {必要|ひつよう}{悪|あく}: a necessary evil

Note: Do not confuse with the reading わるい (bad), which is an i-adjective. {悪|あく} as a noun refers to the abstract concept of evil.
